summary: Construct callable ascending-power polynomial or cubic-spline basis functions.

capability: Construct a list of callable ascending-power polynomial or cubic-spline basis functions.
operation: basis selector and constructor options -> list of callable basis functions
discovery.model: Caller-selected ascending-power polynomial or C2 cubic-spline basis; the polynomial default has three basis functions (powers 0, 1 and 2), while the spline default has five knots and four intervals.
discovery.geometry: One-dimensional scalar abscissa and ordinate samples; the returned evaluators are agnostic to the caller's coherent coordinate and ordinate units.
discovery.boundary: Spline evaluation is zero for finite queries outside the finite knot interval; nonfinite queries are zero-filled. Nonzero endpoint slopes are not a homogeneous basis and are rejected; unsupported factory selections are not approximated.

identity.direction: Declared inputs to List of independent basis evaluators
identity.definition: Construct a list of ascending-power polynomial or cubic-spline evaluators
identity.model: Basis-map selection with poly_deg=3 or n_knots=5 defaults
identity.geometry: one-dimensional scalar abscissa and ordinate samples
identity.boundary: Spline evaluation is zero outside the finite knot interval; no extrapolation is performed.
assumptions: Finite constructor samples and boundary-specific assumptions
Polynomial coefficients are ascending-power columns; poly_deg default3 means three basis functions
Spline keyword defaults n_knots=5,domain=(0,1); xdata/ydata supplied arrays must match
Clamped spline bases require yp=0; nonzero slopes define an affine family, not a linear basis
The second-clamped default basis omits the origin identity column and therefore has n_knots-1 columns
Finite queries outside the closed knot interval and nonfinite query values use the zero-fill convention

outputs.name: basis_fns
outputs.constraints: Polynomial or spline callables; spline callables zero-fill finite values outside the closed knot interval and nonfinite queries

preconditions: Finite constructor samples and boundary-specific assumptions
Polynomial coefficients are ascending-power columns; poly_deg default3 means three basis functions
Spline keyword defaults n_knots=5,domain=(0,1); xdata/ydata supplied arrays must match
Clamped spline bases require yp=0; nonzero slopes define an affine family, not a linear basis
The second-clamped default basis omits the origin identity column and therefore has n_knots-1 columns
Finite queries outside the closed knot interval and nonfinite query values use the zero-fill convention
supported: Finite polynomial and spline basis selections implemented by scirel.geometry.basis
excluded: Quartic and special-function factory selections are rejected; no invented implementations
Physical special-spline closures and unsupported knot domains remain unresolved
Nonzero endpoint slopes for clamped basis construction are rejected
Nonfinite query values are outside the numerical qualification; the implementation zero-fills them as a compatibility convention

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises KeyError for an unregistered selector, NotImplementedError for an unsupported retained selector, TypeError for an unknown keyword, and ValueError for invalid spline samples/knots/boundary parameters; linear-system failures propagate. Nonzero clamped endpoint slopes raise ValueError because they define an affine family.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Numerical linear-algebra or optional SciPy special-function exceptions propagate from evaluation.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; basis construction and evaluation are direct computations without an iterative convergence claim.
failure_semantics.partial_results: A failed constructor returns no evaluator; finite values outside the knot interval and nonfinite query values follow the zero-fill convention.

example.description: Build the default ascending-power polynomial evaluators and evaluate all three at x=0.5.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry.basis import build_basis

evaluators = build_basis()
assert len(evaluators) == 3
np.testing.assert_allclose([fn(0.5) for fn in evaluators], [1.0, 0.5, 0.25])
example.expected: Three evaluators are returned; their values at 0.5 are [1.0, 0.5, 0.25].
